clue.text: Can briefly attempt to acquire self esteem in class

indicators.note: briefly means the word Can is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the clue word itself, before shortening

indicators.note: to acquire means the word for attempt takes in the self-esteem word

parts.note: an attempt is a try
ego is a sense of self-worth

explanation.surface: A tin, it seems, is trying to gain confidence in a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb or a tin, but 'briefly' simply docks its last letter; 'self esteem' is the stock crossword ego.
explanation.definitionFit: A class and this word are synonyms: both mean a group of things sharing a type.

clue.text: Part of magic act uses plant

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A conjuring trick that uses a pot plant as its prop.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'magiC ACT USes'.
explanation.definitionFit: This spiny desert succulent is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Worthwhile to net bucks and withdraw from fight

indicators.note: bucks means the letters jump about like a bucking horse, landing in a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: It's worth netting some cash by pulling out of a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bucks' looks like money to net, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom comes from boxing, where a second throws a towel into the ring to concede, so it means surrendering a contest.

clue.text: Good skin's hard work!

parts.note: rind is the tough skin of fruit or cheese

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that skincare is a real effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A grind is tedious, laborious toil, an idiomatic sense of hard work.

clue.text: Terrible driver takes zero notice cutting right hand turn going north

indicators.note: cutting means the zero and notice letters slice into the right-hand letters

parts.note: O looks like zero
an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means the turn word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A bad motorist ignores the signs and cuts across a right turn heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right hand turn' reads as one driving manoeuvre, but it splits: 'right hand' is one abbreviation and 'turn' a separate word that 'going north' flips, as down clues read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an idiom for a selfish, reckless motorist who hogs the road.

clue.text: Tears fringes off rug to see insect

indicators.note: taking the fringes off a word strips its outer letters, leaving the middle of Tears

parts.note: rug is slang for a toupee or hairpiece, a wig

explanation.surface: Someone trims the tassels off a carpet and spots a bug underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fringes off' leaves EAR from TEARS; 'rug' is informal for a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common garden bug with pincers at its tail, so an example of an insect.

clue.text: A labyrinth's intended, it's said, to create awe

parts.note: a maze is a labyrinth

indicators.note: it's said means the intended word is spoken, giving a sound like the final syllable

parts.note: meant is the past tense of mean, intended

explanation.surface: A labyrinth is designed to leave visitors wonderstruck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' makes MEANT sound like MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe and this noun both name the overwhelming wonder felt at something astonishing.

clue.text: Riding lovely horse following direction for seaside town

indicators.note: following means the riding, lovely and horse words come after the direction

parts.note: west is a compass direction
riding on a horse is being on it
super means excellent, lovely
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A rider on a fine horse heads west to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: WESTON-SUPER-MARE is a seaside resort on the Bristol Channel in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This English resort sits on the coast of the Bristol Channel, so it is a seaside town.

clue.text: Welcome to enter gig free

indicators.note: free means the letters of enter gig are let loose to rearrange

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An invitation to come into a concert without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like no ticket price, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A welcome and this word both name a friendly hello on someone's arrival.

clue.text: Regularly bring in sparkling wine to entertain large street party

indicators.note: to entertain means the wine word holds the picked letters within it

parts.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling wine

indicators.note: Regularly means taking every other letter of the words bring and in

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Bring fizz to a big outdoor celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' picks the even letters across both words 'bring in', so the second 'in' is fodder, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a public festival with processions and dancing through the streets.

clue.text: Harry's smalls wearing well

definitions.note: to harry is to pester or harass, a verb

indicators.note: wearing means the well word has the smalls on, enclosing them

parts.note: hale means healthy, in good health
smalls are underwear; read as two smalls, each abbreviated S

explanation.surface: Harry's underpants are being worn and he feels fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smalls' is British slang for underwear, read here as two small-size abbreviations. Harry looks like a name but is the verb, and 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to bother them persistently, the same as to pester them.

clue.text: Stop queen having sex

parts.note: it is old slang for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A royal is told to cease her love life.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop and to give up doing something are synonyms, as in giving up smoking.

clue.text: Single woman journalist's following peacekeepers

indicators.note: following means the woman and journalist letters come after the peacekeepers

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, which sends peacekeeping forces
ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A lone female reporter is tagging along behind UN troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone single has not married, which is what this adjective means.

clue.text: Tramp accepts employment at home on the water

indicators.note: accepts means the tramp word takes the employment word inside

parts.note: a hobo is a homeless wanderer, a tramp
employment of something is its use

explanation.surface: A vagrant takes a job at home, cosy and settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home' wants to end the wordplay as IN; the definition is the whole phrase 'home on the water'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a vessel fitted out as a dwelling, moored on a river or canal.

clue.text: Finish letters from friend in Greece

indicators.note: letters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Signing off correspondence from a pal abroad in Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'friEND IN Greece'.
explanation.definitionFit: A finish and this word both mean the close or conclusion of something.

clue.text: Misapprehensions when setter replaces article in references

indicators.note: replaces means the setter letter takes the place of the article letter

parts.note: allusions are passing references
A is the indefinite article
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: Mistaken ideas arise when the compiler swaps a grammar word in the citations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaces' swaps the A of ALLUSIONS for I, the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: False beliefs or deceptive impressions are what misapprehensions are, synonyms in the plural.

clue.text: Finally lost sanity in betrayal of the state

indicators.note: Finally takes the closing letter of the word lost

parts.note: reason is soundness of mind, sanity

explanation.surface: A traitor's plot is put down to a final loss of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' takes T from 'lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: This crime is betraying one's country, for example by aiding its enemies or plotting against the sovereign.

clue.text: Idiot put carbon under top secret note on page of old sized paper

indicators.note: under means, in this down clue, the carbon letter sits below the secret letter
on means, in this down clue, the note letter sits above the page letter

parts.note: a fool is an idiot

indicators.note: top means the first letter of the word secret

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
A is a note in the musical scale

explanation.surface: A fool slips carbon paper under a top-secret memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' takes S from 'secret'; 'under' and 'on' place C after S and A before P in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a former British paper size, roughly 13 by 8 inches, used before A4 became standard.

clue.text: Game of strategy's too complicated to grip male students

indicators.note: to grip means the jumbled letters hold the male and students letters inside
complicated means the letters of the word too are tangled into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder
HE is the male pronoun
L is a learner, the L-plate on a learner driver, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A strategy game proves too complex to engage a group of young men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' turns 'too' into OTO, which 'to grip' wraps around the male and students letters; students as learners is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: This board game, also called Reversi, has players flipping black and white discs to outflank each other.

clue.text: Lady's fingers get approval by recognised artist

parts.note: OK is a sign of approval
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist honoured by the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: A woman's hands are praised by a celebrated painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady's fingers' looks like a woman's hands, but it is another name for the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady's fingers is the common British name for this green pod vegetable.

clue.text: Don't slouch, son! These exercises strengthen abs

parts.note: 'sit up!' is the instruction to stop slouching
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent tells their boy to sit straight because it builds stomach muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: These are floor exercises raising the torso from lying, which work the abdominal muscles.

clue.text: Way to secretly watch agent crack

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a hole is a crack or opening

explanation.surface: An undercover operative peeks through a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small peephole in a door or wall, a means of watching unseen.

clue.text: Establish first class record stacking up dishes

indicators.note: stacking up means, in this down clue, the pieces read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to set something is to establish it
A is a first-class grade
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A record is set for piling up crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stacking up' reverses SET + A + LP.
explanation.definitionFit: These are flat dishes for serving or eating food.

clue.text: Service request: allow America to finance hosting Russian leader

parts.note: to let is to allow
US is the United States, America

indicators.note: hosting means the finance word holds the Russian leader inside

parts.note: to finance something is to pay for it

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Russian

explanation.surface: A demand to let the US bankroll a visit from the Kremlin chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes R from 'Russian'; 'hosting' puts it inside PAY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the phrase a minister says to invite a church congregation into prayer, a request during a religious service.

clue.text: A quiet brook's long lost part of spring

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: lost means the long letter goes missing from the brook word

parts.note: a rill is a small stream or brook

explanation.surface: A quiet stream's long-gone stretch, seen in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' drops one L (long) from RILL, leaving RIL. 'spring' is the season, not the water source the brook suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: This month falls in the season of spring in the northern hemisphere, so it is a part of it.

clue.text: Mao and Xi reformed in principle

indicators.note: reformed means the letters of Mao and Xi are formed again in a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Two Chinese leaders are said to have reformed their principles.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth taken as a basic rule is a principle.

clue.text: Dodgy tradesman's bully with young lad

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate, to bully
a boy is a young lad

explanation.surface: A crooked builder's bullying apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy tradesman' is the British informal sense: a builder or plumber who does shoddy work or overcharges.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang this word means an unscrupulous or incompetent workman, not a cattle herder.

clue.text: Party worker after a short time is in command

indicators.note: after means the worker comes after the short-time letters

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
MIN is short for minute, a short time
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A party worker who, after a brief spell, is now the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in command means ruling over others, which is what a dominant person or force does.

clue.text: Spoil sculpture with hard varnish

indicators.note: sculpture means the letters of Spoil are shaped into a new form

parts.note: the anagram fodder
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Ruining a statue by coating it with a tough lacquer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sculpture' reshapes 'Spoil' into POLIS, as a sculptor reshapes material.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, polish and varnish are both coatings that give a surface a shine.

clue.text: Main line during disorder is continuous

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea

indicators.note: during means the line letter sits within the disorder word

parts.note: a mess is a state of disorder

explanation.surface: A main railway line through a chaotic area runs on without a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts L inside MESS, giving MLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without joins or breaks flows smoothly on, so it is unbroken or continuous.
